attempts.summary: Configured node1's crond to run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15, appending output to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log. Fixed two pre-existing defects blocking this: the script file was corrupted (contained leftover heredoc/setup lines instead of just the maintenance logic) and lacked the execute bit, and crond was installed but stopped/not enabled. After remediation, ran the mandatory single-node restart protocol on node1: captured a healthy baseline (boot_id, crond status, cron entry, script perms, log contents), issued a native reboot, polled until exec access returned, confirmed the boot_id changed (proving an actual restart, not just a service bounce), and verified crond auto-started/enabled at boot, the cron entry persisted, the script remained intact and executable, and the log retained pre-restart data while a manual invocation appended a new line successfully.
